description:
Found while writing fz-5xp.14's String module. MINIMAL:

    fnp apply_byte(c, fun), do: <<fun.(c)>>
    apply_byte(97, fn (c) -> c - 32 end)

    error[internal/post-resolution-leftover]: quoted function decode failed:
      invalid any value ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(15), found: ValueKind(3) }
      --> <generated>

Binding the call first is FINE, and is the workaround:

    fnp apply_byte(c, fun) do
      b = fun.(c)
      <<b>>            # "A"
    end

So the segment expression is where it breaks: a closure CALL is not accepted
where the same value from a variable is. A direct call is not affected --
`<<upcase_byte(c)>>` compiles -- so it is specifically the closure-call form
inside a segment.

The error is the same contentless one as fz-5xp.65: no module, no function, no
line, and a ValueKind mismatch that names nothing a reader can act on. Three
different mistakes now produce it.

IMPACT: it forces a `map_bytes(s, fun)` helper -- the natural way to write
upcase/downcase/replace_invalid over bytes -- to be written as a direct
recursion per operation instead.
title: A closure call inside a bitstring segment fails to compile, with no diagnostic
